what: VeriSign operates the .com and .net domain name registries. Every .com domain in the world is registered through its database, and it charges a fee for each one, each year, under a contract with the US government and ICANN.
customers: Domain registrars such as GoDaddy, which resell domains to the businesses and individuals who use them.
money: annual fees on .com and .net domain registrations
moat: A contract granting it exclusive operation of .com, the most valuable namespace on the internet, with a renewal presumption and permitted price increases written in.
risks: The total number of .com domains has been roughly flat for several years
Its contract terms are set by government and ICANN, not the market
Debt of about $1.8 billion against under $500 million of cash
Growth of about 6% comes mostly from price increases
opportunities: Operating margin of 68% and net margin of 50%, among the highest of any public company
Contracted price increases provide revenue growth without any new customers
It buys back shares consistently, so earnings per share rise faster than revenue
watch: Domain name base growth and the permitted price increase schedule.
